newsitem.title: UK: Gehe evaluates position over Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Gehe evaluates position over Lloyds.

text.p: German pharmeceutical wholesaler Gehe said on Friday the company is evaluating its position after UniChem renewed its bid for Lloyds Chemists and added that it is still interested in acquiring Lloyds.
Dieter Kammerer, chairman of the management board of Gehe said: "We welcome the announcement that we have satisfied the DTI and we are evaluating our position."

"We believe that UniChem would face significant risks in acquiring Lloyds Chemists given the relative size of the two companies and UniChem's lack of experience in integrating major acquisitions," said Kammerer.
"This is especially true in the light of Lloyds Chemists' reduced profitability and the reduced potential for synergies as a result of the DTI's (Department of Trade and Industry) ruling."
Gehe questioned UniChem's claim that its acquisition of Lloyds will enhance earnings after the first 12 months.
In a statement to the London stock exchange Gehe also asked if UniChem had the experience to integrate Lloyds Chemists effectively and questioned the consistency of UniChem's recent statement.

Earlier the DTI cleared the way for the acquisition of Lloyds after accepting pledges from both rival bidders, UniChem and Gehe AG, that they would sell off certain Lloyds' wholesale businesses within three months of the completed merger.
UniChem has pledged to sell the wholesaling businesses operated by Lloyds from the depots at Cambridge, Carlisle, Coulsdon, Derby, Glasgow and York.
In addition to these, GEHE has promised the authorities that it would sell Lloyds' depot business at Belfast.

Lloyds Chemists, owns the second largest chain of retail pharmacies in Britain with more than 900 outlets. UniChem is one of the two largest wholesalers of pharmaceutical products in Britain and also owns a chain of some 400 retail pharmacies called Moss Chemists.
Gehe, Europe's largest drug distributor, is keen to expand its pharmaceutical retail business in Britain which it entered with the acquisition of AAH Plc in April.
